# Data Model

## Definition

A Data Model is a structured representation of data — its entities, attributes, relationships and constraints — at a stated level of abstraction and for a stated purpose.

## Explanation

"Data model" is an umbrella term. A model is only meaningful when its **level** is explicit. This knowledge base distinguishes four model levels, each belonging to an [[Architecture Layer]]:

| Model | Layer | Answers |
|---|---|---|
| [[Conceptual Data Model]] | Conceptual | Which things matter and how they relate? |
| [[Information Model]] | Information | How is meaning represented, paradigm-independent? |
| [[Logical Data Model]] | Logical | How is it structured in a paradigm (relational, dimensional, graph)? |
| [[Physical Data Model]] | Physical | How is it realized in a specific store? |

Meaning itself is defined in the [[Semantic Model]], not in the data model ([[Meaning Before Representation]]).

## Distinctions

- A data model is not a database schema; a schema is one realization of a physical model.
- A data model is not a [[Semantic Model]]: data models represent meaning, semantic models define it.

## Examples

- An ER diagram of Party, Agreement and Product (conceptual).
- A star schema with a Sales fact and Customer dimension (logical, dimensional paradigm).
